newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF cuts margin requirements on contracts again.
newsitem.headline: MATIF cuts margin requirements on contracts again.

text.p: French futures and options exchange MATIF SA said on Wednesday it was reducing initial margin requirements and daily fluctuation limits for its French bond, Ecu bond and PIBOR futures contracts because of declining volatility in the run-up to European monetary union.
MATIF last trimmed margin requirements and daily limits on July 2, 1996.

"This reduction is due to the low level of volatility since the middle of 1996 resulting from the process of convergence towards the euro which has stabilised European interest rate markets," MATIF said in a statement.

The new initial margins, the amount MATIF requires from clients when opening futures positions, will be effective from April 25. The new daily fluctation limits will take effect starting April 28, MATIF said in a statement.
The initial margin for French franc bond futures will be reduced to 7,500 francs from 12,500 francs previously, while the fluctuation limit will be reduced to 140 basis points from 200.
Initial margins for Ecu bond futures contracts will be cut to 1,500 Ecu from 2,500 Ecu and the fluctuation limit will be trimmed to 140 basis points from 200.
The initial margin for PIBOR contracts will be halved to 5,000 francs and the daily fluctuation limit cut to 35 basis points from 60 basis points previously.
